A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same spectral framework and denoising work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting. An internal metric-label inconsistency in v2 limits one result comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic simulations, ResNet18/CIFAR-10 sampling experiments, and analyses comparing vision-model representations with primate V2 recordings.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and neural-data results and adds eigenvalue-control experiments, MLE confidence-interval examples, and numerical localization-threshold tests.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains population-spectrum fitting, self-overlap computation, and constrained overlap recovery; the truncated-SVD alternative also remains. Appendix G adds an alternative likelihood-based overlap estimator, demonstrated in Fig. S4, alongside the original constrained least-squares procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds an explicitly evaluated exponential-spectrum population, whereas v1's reported synthetic experiments use power-law spectra. The CIFAR-10/ResNet18 and primate V2 coverage remains; newly cited human fMRI work is not a new evaluated dataset.

E2.justification: The estimator comparisons retain raw sample similarities and population/theoretical references. Newly discussed general-spectrum and moment-based estimators are not benchmarked against the proposed method. Appendix F's hybrid CKA is a component-control analysis rather than a competing denoising baseline.

E3.justification: The main synthetic comparison changes population similarity from 1 to approximately 0.5. New analyses introduce population-eigenvalue substitution controls at P=100 and a PR≈2 criterion for localization thresholds. The reported neural setting remains N=20 of 103 neurons; changed scatter plots do not establish an undocumented protocol revision.

E4.justification: New Appendix F isolates eigenvector effects by combining population eigenvalues with sample eigenvectors, testing the claimed mechanism under power-law and exponential spectra. Appendix H/Fig. S7 adds quantitative tests of the localization-threshold prediction across neuron counts, stimulus counts, and spectral exponents, beyond v1's descriptive localization plots.

E5.justification: v1 shows error bars and sampling variability but lacks the new inferential uncertainty framework. Appendix G adds single- and multiple-trial profile-likelihood intervals, Fisher/delta-method intervals for CKA/CCA, and five-trial 95% bands in Fig. S4. The matched overlap heatmap also changes explicitly from single-trial to five-trial averaging.

E6.justification: The main synthetic curves are replaced under approximately 0.5 rather than unit population similarity, and overlap heatmaps change with averaging. New results appear in Figs. S2–S4 and S7. The V2 cortex scatter values also change substantially, but v2 Fig. 5 labels its right-panel axes CKA while the caption specifies CCA, preventing reliable metric matching.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds a probabilistic overlap model and confidence-interval derivations. Appendix H adds a two-peak support-merger approximation yielding i*≈(1+γ)√N/√8. Appendix C also revises the Stieltjes-transform derivation, including replacing v1's g′≫1 truncation condition with βg′≪1. The original overlap framework remains.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion newly elevate the square-root neuron-count law to a principal result for power-law spectra, with quantitative guidance for recording enough neurons to resolve specified components. This expands the contribution beyond the retained sampling-bias explanation and population-similarity recovery claims.

C2.justification: New Section 7 specifies limitations involving Gaussian linear projections, non-Gaussian dependencies, symmetry assumptions, and dynamic or nonlinear metrics. Section 4.2.2 newly acknowledges that moment-based CKA estimation is better suited to small datasets. These qualify applicability while retaining the original delocalization interpretation and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix D replaces the supplemental-code statement with a GitHub repository link and specifies a single A100 GPU; acknowledgments identify the computing cluster. Appendix G supplies procedural pseudocode for confidence intervals. These improve documented access and implementation detail without establishing changes to existing experiment hardware.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Erdélyi, Gauthaman et al., Ledoit and Wolf's 2015 spectrum estimator, Murphy et al., and Pospisil et al.'s shape-distance work. It expands discussion of biological power laws and alternative estimators, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the abstract, notation, theoretical explanations, and backward-inference discussion, updates affiliations, and replaces the Impact Statement with Limitations. Most existing section order and exposition remain recognizable; the new scientific appendices do not themselves constitute wholesale narrative rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one. Existing figures are substantially regrouped: v1 Figs. 1–2 become v2 Fig. 1, Figs. 4–5 become Fig. 3, and Figs. 7–8 become Fig. 4. v2 adds six supplementary figures and two algorithm displays, and redraws the neural scatter plots and legends.

improvement.justification: Appendix C improves the approximation reasoning, Appendix F directly tests the proposed mechanism, and Appendices G–H add conditional uncertainty estimates and quantitative localization guidance. Explicit limitations and code/hardware disclosures improve transparency. However, unexplained changes to the real-data scatter values and Fig. 5's CKA/CCA labeling conflict weaken an important empirical comparison, limiting the overall gain.
